page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak and poor categories respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression also registers as poor. However, the instance leverages its 16 dedicated physical cores to achieve average multi-core performance, as demonstrated by stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU benchmarks. Memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks remains in the average tier, though PassMark memory scores are weak.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1ne.4xlarge offers a high density of memory relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. The instance is suited for database operations, Redis SET operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded decompression tasks. It can also handle light LLM inference for small models, though performance drops to weak when processing prompts on medium-sized 7B models.
